item.description: NEW YORK, Nov 19 : Alibaba was sued on Thursday in New York by shareholders who accused the Chinese e-commerce giant of defrauding them by concealing its ties to the suspected Chinese spy whose relationship with former Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang contributed to his resignation last week.According to a

Alibaba defrauded shareholders by concealing ties to suspected spy in Nvidia scandal, lawsuit says

People walk past the Alibaba booth during the World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) in Shanghai, China, July 17, 2026. REUTERS/Go Nakamura/ File photo

FAST

NEW YORK, Nov 19 : Alibaba was sued on Thursday in New York by shareholders who accused the Chinese e-commerce giant of defrauding them by concealing its ties to the suspected Chinese spy whose relationship with former Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang contributed to his resignation last week. According to a proposed class action filed in Manhattan federal court, Alibaba inflated its share price by knowingly and materially understating in its 2024, 2025 and 2026 annual reports the risks that actual or suspected export control violations could harm its business. Shareholders cited Alibaba's relationship with Megaspeed, a Singaporean company suspected of helping Beijing gain access to advanced Nvidia AI chips, and whose executive Alice Huang had a relationship with Jensen Huang, who is not related to her. The shareholders said Alibaba shares fell 14 per cent over four days last week because of media reports on Alibaba's ties to Alice Huang and Megaspeed, including that Alibaba had become Megaspeed's "dominant" customer.

They attributed part of the decline to a November 12 Reuters article that said Nvidia's spy scandal could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on Chinese AI companies' remote use of advanced processors. Alibaba did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Eddie Wu, its chief executive, is also a defendant. Nvidia itself faces several shareholder lawsuits over the spy scandal, including allegations of lax oversight by its directors. Wu said on Thursday that Alibaba remained on track for $100 billion in external cloud revenue and a 20 per cent EBITDA margin by 2030, despite US curbs on access to computing power that could affect the company's products and services next year. The restrictions were imposed after Huang resigned from Nvidia. In June, Alibaba sued the US government over being added to a blacklist of "Chinese military companies" that the Department of Defense linked to that country's military. Last month, a federal judge in California granted Alibaba an injunction barring the US government from denying Pentagon contracts to companies whose lobbyists also work with designated Chinese military companies. Alibaba said that restriction caused its lobbyists to retreat because they feared losing other clients, and violated its First Amendment constitutional right to speak to and petition the government. Thursday's lawsuit by Alibaba shareholder Withida Bihan seeks unspecified damages for holders of Alibaba's American depositary shares between May 23, 2024 and November 11, 2026.

Source: Reuters

ＶＷ、労組へ2年間給与据え置きや週35時間労働の見直しを提示 8:07 配信

独ボルフスブルクにあるフォルクスワーゲン本社工場。2024年10月28日撮影。REUTERS/Axel Schmidt（ロイター） Rachel More　Christina Amann

[ベルリン １９日 ロイター] - ドイツの自動車大手フォルクスワーゲン（ＶＷ）は１９日、２４日に始まる労使交渉に向け、２年間の給与水準の据え置きや、現金または追加休暇としてあてがう賞与（ボーナス）の廃止などの賃金協定の見直しを労働組合側に提示した。またドイツ最大の産業別労働組合ＩＧメタルが勝ち取った週３５時間労働についても再交渉を求め、賃金を据え置いたまま労働時間を延長することを要求した。

労組の首席交渉担当者トルステン・グレーガー氏は「ＶＷの経営陣は従業員を裏切っている」と反発し、「これは会社に深い傷跡を残す、過酷で苦い、そして消耗させる激しい対立になるだろう」との認識を示した。労使対立が激化している中で、労組は来年１月以降にストライキを実施すると警告した。

オリバー・ブルーメ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が打ち出した１０万人の人員削減計画などの構造改革を受け、労使関係は緊張状態にある。

労使交渉で話し合う賃金協定の見直しはＶＷの従業員約１２万人に影響する。開催場所の北西部エムデンには、構造改革の一環として２０３０年代初頭以降に閉鎖する可能性がある４つの工場のうち１つが立地する。

ドイツの自動車メーカーは、欧州で勢いを伸ばしている電気自動車（ＥＶ）メーカーの比亜迪（ＢＹＤ）などの中国企業に押されて業績が悪化している。中国企業は欧州市場で１０％を超えるシェアを獲得している。

item.description: The US approved shipments of AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD to companies on the Pentagon's list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

World

US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months, House committee says

The US approved shipments of AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD to companies on the Pentagon's list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies.

An Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) artificial intelligence chip is displayed at the San Jose McEnery Convention Center, in San Jose, California, US, on Jun 12, 2025. (File photo: Reuters/Max A. Cherney)

20 Nov 2026 07:04AM (Updated: 20 Nov 2026 07:10AM)

FAST

WASHINGTON: The Trump administration approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, the House Foreign Affairs Committee said on Thursday (Nov 19). The approvals for 879,000 chip shipments by the Commerce Department included 75,000 for Alibaba, 150,000 for Tencent, 43,000 for Baidu, and 4,000 for BYD, all on the Pentagon's list of alleged Chinese military-backed companies , the committee noted. The unusual release of chip export licensing data comes as the administration of President Donald Trump faces heightened scrutiny following news about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy , which has fueled renewed calls in Washington for a tougher stance on China. Companies had sought permission to ship over 3.4 million chips to China during the period, the documents showed. It was not immediately clear how many of the approvals resulted in actual China-bound shipments of chips, which included Nvidia's H200 and AMD's equivalent MI325X.

News surrounding Huang has turned a spotlight on instances of Nvidia AI chips being smuggled to China that went unpunished, dialing up pressure on the Trump administration to crack down on Chinese tech threats. "The fact that over 30 per cent of the AI chips sent to China were shipped to companies that the Department of War has designated as Chinese military companies is astonishing, and calls into question whether Commerce conducted any serious national security review before approving these licenses,” said Chris McGuire, a former US official and expert on the US-China technology battle. Nvidia said in a statement that the approvals were "subject to strict conditions and limited volumes." It added that "despite receiving some licenses, we have since stopped shipping H200s to China". AMD said it "complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations". Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu, BYD, the Commerce Department and the Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Also read:

Nvidia faces deepening scrutiny over China chip ties, CEO affair

Why Alibaba, Baidu and BYD are on Pentagon’s list of 'Chinese military companies'

MOST DETAILED PUBLIC DISCLOSURE Former President Joe Biden had restricted Chinese access to the prized chips over fears that they would supercharge China's military and erode the US lead in artificial intelligence. But Trump in December gave the green light for Nvidia to ship its H200 chip to China, rolling back Biden-era restrictions and drawing fierce criticism from China hawks across the US political spectrum. Despite the approvals, questions swirled as to whether the AI chips were actually reaching Chinese shores. In May, Reuters reported the US had cleared about 10 companies to buy the H200, but that no deliveries had taken place. In testimony before the committee in July, Commerce Department official Jeffrey Kessler said shipments had begun but there had been 'very few'. Several major Chinese internet companies had each obtained about 10,000 H200 chips, Reuters has since reported, citing people familiar with the matter. "This is the most detailed public disclosure in the history of the Export Control Reform Act," committee Chair Brian Mast, a Republican from Florida, said upon releasing the data, referring to 2018 legislation that expanded Commerce's authority to restrict the export of sensitive technologies for national security reasons.

Source: Reuters/co

Archaeologist and conservator Lilian Vega de Zea handles restored stucco heads from the Maya Classic Period that were unearthed at El Mirador archaeological site in the Peten region of Guatemala, in the restoration laboratory of the Cuenca Mirador Archaeological Project in Guatemala City, Guatemala, November 19, 2026. FAST

GUATEMALA CITY, Nov 19 : Guatemala has unveiled several expressive, life-sized stucco heads crafted in the Maya period, offering the public a look at what researchers say is a unique concentration of such sculptures from the Maya world. Dating from the seventh and eighth centuries, the pieces are part of a bigger collection unearthed at the Mirador Basin archaeological site in northern Guatemala in a series of digs over the last decade, impressing researchers with their artistry, state of preservation and the size of the collection. “There is not a single known example anywhere in the Mayan world of such a large number of sculptures recovered from a single structure,” said Douglas Mauricio, an archaeologist at the Mirador Basin Project. Major Maya cities grew in prominence beginning 3,000 years ago across a large swathe of present-day southern Mexico and several Central American nations, during a period marked by advances in mathematics, astronomy and art.

The elaborate carvings — showing expressions ranging from scrunched foreheads to broad smiles — highlight the Maya people's mastery of a wide range of artistic skills beyond the mathematics and astronomy for which they are known, said Lilian Vega de Zea, restoration director for the Mirador Basin Project. “It shows us the advanced technology they had in everything," she said. The use of colors indicated a complex process involving multiple people — some who prepared the colors, others who mixed the stucco, and a person serving as a model for the head itself, Vega de Zea said. “These heads represent important people ... they also served as a message to the society of the time, depicting someone who held a certain level of authority.” The sculptures offer clues about a later period of Maya occupation at El Mirador, when a smaller population returned to the site centuries after its Preclassic peak and maintained the earlier pieces in good condition, Mauricio said. "They continued to preserve, protect, and hold their Preclassic ancestors in high regard," Mauricio said.

Source: Reuters

item.title: India's wheat acreage may see steepest fall in 26 years on water shortage
item.description: Weak monsoon rains have prompted farmers in key growing states to shift to less water-intensive crops such as chickpeas, raising concerns over wheat output and food inflation ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Industry / Agriculture / India's wheat acreage may see steepest fall in 26 years on water shortage

India's wheat acreage may see steepest fall in 26 years on water shortage Weak monsoon rains have prompted farmers in key growing states to shift to less water-intensive crops such as chickpeas, raising concerns over wheat output and food inflation

India's main winter-sown crop, wheat usually competes for acreage with rapeseed, chickpeas and corn (Photo: PTI)

Reuters JALNA 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 20 2026 | 12:14 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India's wheat acreage is poised for its steepest decline in 26 years as fields parched by the weakest monsoon rains in more than a decade spur farmers to switch to competing crops in search of better returns, industry officials told Reuters. The drop in planting, coupled with the risk of lower yields brought by a severe El Niño weather pattern, threatens to curb output in the world's second-largest wheat producer, in turn boosting prices and complicating efforts to damp food inflation. "Wheat needs to be irrigated at least four to five times, but we don't have enough water even to sow the crop," said farmer Vilas Bhutekar in the Jalna district of the western state of Maharashtra.   "So we chose chickpeas instead, as they require less water." India's main winter-sown crop, wheat usually competes for acreage with rapeseed, chickpeas and corn. Also Read

Wheat sowing down 15% so far; overall rabi crops coverage falls 11%

A month after lifting of ban, wheat exports rise fourfold, shows data premium

PM-Kisan 24th instalment: PM Modi to release ₹18,680 crore on October 30

Wheat sowing lags at 11,000 ha amid deficient monsoon, irrigation concerns

Wheat acreage likely to remain steady despite weak monsoon rainfall

India's June-September monsoon rains were the lowest in more than a decade as the drying effect of the El Niño drove rainfall as much as 41 per cent below average in key wheat-growing states such as Punjab, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. "Wheat needs more water than other competing crops," said Nitin Gupta, deputy country head at agricultural trader Olam Agri India. "But water is in short supply in some regions this year, which could mean farmers plant less wheat." Wheat was planted across 5 million hectares (12 million acres) by Nov. 13, down 15.3 per cent from a year earlier, government data show. Planting for the 2026/27 season is expected to fall about 6 per cent from last year's record of 33.6 million hectares (83 million acres), an average estimate by 10 industry officials shows. That would be the steepest decline since 2000/01, taking area under the crop to the lowest in four years at 31.58 million hectares (78 million acres). Crop shift Wheat acreage is expected to stay largely steady in the key northern states of Haryana and Punjab, which have access to reliable irrigation. But farmers in other states are likely to shift from wheat to less-thirsty crops such as chickpea and rapeseed, industry officials said. Prices of these crops have risen much more than wheat, prompting farmers to shift acreage away from the grain, said Sandeep Bansal, director of a flour miller based in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh. "Wheat is usually farmers' first choice, but this year other crops are giving better returns," Bansal said. The state-run Food Corporation of India buys wheat from farmers at the minimum support price, which New Delhi raised this year by just 1 per cent to 2,610 rupees per 100 kg, the smallest increase since 2002/03. "The government typically incentivises wheat planting by raising procurement prices by 5 to 6 per cent annually," said a New Delhi-based trader with a global trade house. "This year's 1 per cent hike is, in fact, discouraging farmers from expanding wheat acreage."

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.description:
Michael S. Derby
[ニューヨーク １９日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のバー理事は１９日...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＦＲＢの金融規制見直し、将来の市場混乱対応能力弱める恐れ＝バー理事 7:36 配信

米連邦準備理事会（FRB）のバー理事。2月17日、ニューヨークで撮影。REUTERS/Brendan McDermid（ロイター） Michael S. Derby

[ニューヨーク １９日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のバー理事は１９日、ＦＲＢで進められている金融規制見直しが、将来の市場混乱の兆候を把握して対応する能力を弱める恐れがあるとの懸念を示した。

バー氏はトランプ大統領の２期目が始まった２０２５年初めまでＦＲＢの金融監督担当トップを務めていたが、ＦＲＢの独立性を維持するためとして同職を退いた。後任のボウマン氏は説明責任の向上を掲げる規制緩和策を推進しているが、一部では監督に抜け穴が生じかねないとの声も出ている。

こうした規制見直しについてバー氏は「足元で直ちに問題になるとは考えていない」と語りつつも「長期的な影響や結果を伴う。監督体制が徐々に弱体化し、銀行システムの安全性が低下する可能性がある」と警告した。

またワシントンに勤務するＦＲＢの銀行監督担当職員の約３分の１が削減対象となっていると明らかにした上で、０７－０９年の世界金融危機当時、ＦＲＢには問題を迅速に発見・分析できる十分な人材が不足していたと振り返った。

バー氏は「個々の変更が直ちにリスクをもたらすわけではないが、こうした動きが積み重なることに懸念がある。警戒すべきリスクは存在する」と強調。過去１年半にわたり、ＦＲＢの監督・規制政策の方向性について自身の反対意見を公に表明してきたとも語った。

金融政策については、追加利上げが必要になるとの見方を改めて示すとともに「インフレ率は依然として高過ぎる。金融政策をさらに調整する必要があると思う」と訴えた。

ＦＲＢは１２月８─９日に次回の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）を開催する。市場では政策金利を２５ベーシスポイント引き上げるとの見方が有力。その後も物価上昇圧力の抑制に向け、来年に追加利上げが実施されると予想されている。

Australia's NextDC shareholders deliver second pay strike but stop short of board spill

FILE PHOTO: The NextDC S6 data centre stands in Sydney, Australia, June 22, 2026. REUTERS/Hollie Adams/File Photo

FAST

Nov 20 : Shareholders of Australian data centre developer NextDC rejected its executive pay plan for a second straight year but voted against removing the board, a stock exchange filing showed on Friday. Investors holding 72.06 per cent of shares voted against the remuneration report, broadly matching last year's near 72 per cent opposition, amid calls for greater accountability and closer alignment between executive pay and shareholder returns. Under Australia's "two strikes" rule, opposition of at least 25 per cent to a pay report in two consecutive years triggers a vote on whether to remove the board and force directors to stand for re-election. However, 96.21 per cent of votes cast opposed the board spill, allowing directors to remain in place while keeping pressure on them to address investor concerns over executive pay.

The votes come nearly a month after CEO Craig Scroggie said he would forgo his fiscal 2027 bonus and the company withdrew a plan to increase the non-executive directors' maximum aggregate annual remuneration. "The M3 issues have hit confidence, and when a big project stumbles, shareholders want to see pay take the hit across the board, not just one line item," Mark Gardener, CEO of MPC Markets, said. NextDC lifted its annual net revenue and underlying operating earnings outlook on Friday, driven by strong sales and revenue growth outside the affected M3 contracts, alongside cost-saving measures. That followed last month's cut to its earnings forecast and capital expenditure plans, and a pause on all projects lacking customer contracts after a major setback at its flagship M3 data centre in Melbourne. NextDC shares ended 7.1 per cent lower at A$9.01, marking its weakest session since October 23, and tracked the broader technology sub-index, which ended 4.7 per cent lower. The market cares more about the earnings path than the pay fight, and the guidance upgrade on growth outside M3, along with cost savings, tells investors the core business is working, Gardener said. ($1 = 1.5011 Australian dollars)

Source: Reuters

item.title: Anthropic set to begin trading as a US$1.5-trillion company in the biggest IPO on record
item.description: Anthropic is set to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday after pricing its IPO at US$83 per share, valuing the artificial intelligence giant at $1.5 trillion and surpassing SpaceX as the largest ...
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.content:encoded: NEW YORK — The artificial intelligence giant Anthropic opened for trading Thursday in the biggest public stock offering ever, despite investor fears of a possible AI bubble and public anxiety that the technology threatens lives and livelihoods. Anthropic shares began trading at US$111.50, spiking more than 30 per cent above the initial public offering price, before closing at US$97.17, more than 17 per cent higher than the IPO. A day earlier, the company priced its IPO at US$83 per share, enough to value the entire business at US$1.5 trillion, surpassing SpaceX as the largest IPO on record. At the start of trading, the valuation leaped to US$2.01 trillion. The initial price was surprisingly high given that investor worries had ratcheted up even more recently following the stunning ouster of AI’s chief promoter, the CEO of Nvidia, in a possible Chinese spying scandal. Anthropic had earlier set a much lower price range between US$70 to US$78 per share. “It’s a big win for the tech sector after a white-knuckle time with Nvidia,” said Dan Ives, a financial analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co. “The pricing shows strong demand among investors.” A big test remains if investors maintain the classic “IPO pop” by keeping the stock aloft in its first day — or if it will tumble by the close. The San Francisco-based maker of the Claude AI tool offered 980 million shares to the public, which at US$83 per share translated into proceeds of US$81 billion. Anthropic’s soaring debut on Wall Street was not enough to carry the rest of the market. U.S. stock indexes fell after a morning rally quickly evaporated. IPO offers a way to raise money without going deeper into debt In addition to market jitters over AI, the IPO is facing down a potential regulatory crackdown by a Democratic-led Congress next year and growing anti-AI sentiment among the public. For its part, Anthropic rival OpenAI decided to postpone its initial offering until next year. The company, trading under the ticker symbol ANT, is also facing big financial challenges ahead. Anthropic already has taken on US$6.2 billion in debt, which it acknowledges in financial filings is “substantial.” Adding to the strain, the company is unprofitable, at least under standard accounting rules, suggesting that its resources to pay interest and principal are limited. While the company showed ample cash in its last financial report, it would have likely run through it quickly given its outsize spending plans. In the same financial report, the company said it had signed leases and other deals requiring it to spend US$900 billion on computing power and infrastructure in the coming years, including US$70 billion in the next 12 months. Such massive spending by AI companies, comparable to the Gilded Age splurge on railroads, have scared lenders, helping to push borrowing rates high recently. With the IPO, though, Anthropic will now have enormous resources to accelerate its expansion without taking on more debt. The offering will also allow its employees to sell vested stock, making many of them millionaires overnight — and potentially adding billions of dollars to the fortunes of CEO Dario Amodei and his sister, Anthropic President Daniela Amodei. AI industry faces concerns about data centres, a possible bubble and regulations Founded five years ago by the siblings along with several other former OpenAI veterans, Anthropic is locked in a fight for dominance with that company. But both companies have plenty of other competitors, including Google, startups in the U.S. and China and SpaceX, which has an AI business. Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX’s AI division have all lost more money than they’ve made because of the huge costs associated with building AI. That has fueled growing concerns about a bubble forming in the sector. Dario Amodei cautioned in September that the AI industry should slow its fast-moving development to give safety measures time to catch up. Without such a slowdown, Amodei warned, AI could be capable of letting loose a swarm of agents that could take over the internet within months. In comments at the opening bell Thursday, Amodei sought to dampen fears by stressing a commitment to ensure humans are in control of the technology. “If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same,” he said. ”The goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.” Amid mounting fears, the regulatory environment could change for Anthropic once the new Congress is in session. Newly elected Democrats are vowing to crack down on the industry as a backlash unfolds against data centres. And two big states offering incentives for data centres, Texas and Georgia, just elected Democratic governors who have vowed to stop new construction. In his comments Thursday, Amodei also touted a range of positive uses for AI, noting that Claude already is helping scientists do quicker research and that the technology could help accelerate that progress in the future. “Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox and polio history for most of the world,” he said, “but progress in other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families.” He also pointed to Claude’s use across companies, nonprofits and government services. “I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future,” he said. Adding to the pressure to go public was the possibility that demand for AI shares could drop or even collapse. Investors have become anxious about the massive financing needs of the sector, and several tech companies have pulled IPO plans recently. Market valuation for AI companies is going to be “up and down for many years to come, but more up than down,” said Rich Lesser, the global chair and former CEO of Boston Consulting Group. “Exactly what the flow of that will be, it’s very hard to predict,” Lesser said Tuesday in an interview with The Associated Press at the Semafor Silicon Valley & the World forum. “There’s no question what Anthropic and OpenAI and Google and a number of the other players in this industry have done is pretty remarkable.” ___ Bernard Condon and Barbara Ortutay, The Associated Press Ortutay reported from Oakland, California. Associated Press business writers Kaitlyn Huamani in Los Angeles and Michelle Chapman in New York contributed.

item.title: Four men guilty of sex crimes against woman drugged by husband in UK case with echoes of Pelicot
item.description: Her ex-husband, Philip Young, admitted to more than 50 offences, including rape and sharing recordings of the abuse online.
item.dc:creator: CNA

Four men guilty of sex crimes against woman drugged by husband in UK case with echoes of Pelicot

Her ex-husband, Philip Young, admitted to more than 50 offences, including rape and sharing recordings of the abuse online.

Joanne Young looks on outside Winchester Crown Court after a jury returned guilty verdicts in the case of all four men accused of raping or sexually abusing her while she was drugged by her then-husband between 2016 and 2023, in Winchester, Britain, November 19, 2026. REUTERS/Jack Taylor TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY

FAST

WINCHESTER: Four British men were convicted on Thursday (Nov 19) of raping or sex ually abusing a woman who was drugged by her then- husband in a case with echoes of that of Gisele Pelicot , the French woman who became a global symbol in the fight against sex ual violence. Joanne Young, like Pelicot , decided to waive her legal right to anonymity after discovering that her husband at the time had repeatedly drugged her and advertised her for sex online to strangers over more than a decade. Philip Young, a 50-year-old former local councillor, pleaded guilty in January to more than 50 charges against his ex-wife, including 11 counts of rape and charges relating to recording the abuse and publishing it online hundreds of times. "This abuse has cost me my life as I knew it," Joanne Young said outside court. "The person I trusted most in the world betrayed me in the most horrific way."

CALL TO RECONSIDER LAW ON CONSENT Police discovered the abuse only after an account linked to Philip Young posted bestiality images online in 2024 and then seized his devices, containing videos and images of the abuse. Young's crimes have striking similarities to those of Dominique Pelicot , who admitted drugging his then-wife Gisele and inviting dozens of men to rape her, prompting a 2024 trial that horrified the world and spurred France to revamp its rape law. Britain's National Crime Agency said this year it had uncovered a "truly international network" of drug-facilitated rape and sex ual assault, which it said was organised online and had members across the world. Law enforce men t officials from 10 countries, including the US, are now working on a global operation to target drug-facilitated sex ual assaults. Joanne Young said her case "raises serious questions about how the law deals with consent", adding: "I urge the govern men t to look at this as a priority so that wo men are properly protected in the future."

Women's rights campaigners outside Winchester Crown Court, where a jury is deliberating in the case of four men accused of raping or sexually assaulting Joanne Young, in Winchester, Britain, Nov 13, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Toby Shepheard)

FIFTH MAN HAD PLEADED GUILTY The men found guilty following a trial at Winchester Crown Court, in southern England, had responded to adverts posted by Philip Young, who admitted drugging his wife and inviting strangers to have sex with her, watching and filming while it happened. Richard Clive Wilkins, 62, was convicted of rape and assault by penetration, Norman Macksoni, 48, was also convicted of rape, Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, was found guilty of sex ual assault and assault by penetration, while Mohammed Hassan, 38, was convicted of one count of sex ual assault. In defences echoing those of many of the 50 co-defendants of Dominique Pelicot who were convicted in France, they said they thought Joanne Young consented and that it was a shared fantasy with her then- husband . She had sat in court as prosecutor Sarah Jones said her ex- husband had posted images online, showing his then-wife tied to her bed and blindfolded, as he "sought strangers to come and sleep with his wife – any age, any race". After the verdicts were announced, Judge Pushpinder Saini said she had shown "amazing bravery". A fifth man, Dean Hamilton, 47, had previously admitted rape, assault by penetration and sex ual assault. All five, along with Philip Young, will be sentenced next month and Saini said they faced a significant custodial sentence.

PELICOT NOT AN ISOLATED CASE The Pelicot trial horrified the world, but it now appears to be far from an isolated case . Specialist Crown Prosecution Service prosecutor James Foster said the case "marks the first time in England that a jury has convicted men of sex ually assaulting a woman , who had been drugged in abuse organised by her husband ". In April, law enforce men t bodies from 10 countries, coordinated by Europol, the EU's law enforce men t agency, set up "Project Medusa" to tackle the issue, led by investigators from Britain and Germany, and including the US, France and Canada. Those involved have since launched 113 investigations linked to that operation, leading to 57 arrests and 158 safeguarded victims, Europol said in June. The Crown Prosecution Service said British police had spoken with investigators who worked on the Pelicot case and that the toxicology expert whose evidence was used in France had also worked on the case involving Joanne Young. "I live with a pain that's hard to put into words ... it is terrifying that this could happen to anyone," Young said.

Source: Reuters/fs

FAST

Nov 19 : Intuit said on Thursday it has agreed to sell email marketing platform Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, five years after acquiring it for nearly three times more in its largest deal ever. Shares of the TurboTax maker were down 10 per cent after the bell, while those of Bending Spoons shares rose 3 per cent. Intuit said the sale will sharpen its focus on AI-powered products for small businesses, and that it plans to use the cash proceeds to repurchase shares. The company has increasingly focused on integrating artificial intelligence across its products as it seeks to automate tasks for consumers and businesses and expand the range of services it provides.

The deal includes $3.31 billion in cash and $368 million in stock, and is expected to close in early 2027. Intuit acquired Mailchimp in 2021 for about $12 billion, bringing the email marketing platform into its small-business software portfolio. The deal gives Bending Spoons, which went public in July, another major digital business to add to its growing portfolio. The company said it plans to invest substantially in the marketing platform and pursue changes to its technology, products, marketing and monetization. "Mailchimp has helped millions of businesses grow and acquire customers through email marketing automation," said Jack Tam, senior vice president at Intuit. Intuit said that revenue from Mailchimp decreased 1 per cent to $313 million in the first quarter. It also trimmed 2027 forecast and now expects full-year revenue to grow 8 per cent to 9 per cent, compared with its previous forecast for 9 per cent to 10 per cent growth. Intuit said the revised guidance reflects a change to its personal-finance platform Credit Karma, which has seen performance fall below expectations as higher interest rates weighed on growth and a shift in consumer behavior had a faster-than-anticipated impact on the business. The company maintained its full-year operating income and profit guidance.

Source: Reuters

AI surge could strain US capacity and overheat economy, Fed's Goolsbee says

Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee participates in a session titled "The Future of Global Finance" during the Semafor World Economy conference in Washington, D.C., U.S., April 14, 2026. REUTERS/Elizabeth Frantz

FAST

WASHINGTON, Nov 19 : The booming rollout of artificial intelligence technology could strain the US economy's capacity and further boost inflation that the Federal Reserve will have to counteract, Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said on Thursday, as AI firm Anthropic set a new record for an initial public offering of stock. "The AI boom is contributing to the potential of overheating in the economy. I find it hard to ... look at that any other way," Goolsbee said in a conference call with reporters. "When you're getting major business investment, almost unprecedented levels of business investment, there's a high danger that the economy's capacity cannot handle that kind of a pig through the python." Goolsbee said he sees the multitrillion-dollar pipeline of data-center projects already adding to what he referred to as "borderline, disturbingly high inflation rates" that are well above the Fed's 2 per cent target and potentially heading higher. He said he felt the Anthropic IPO, giving the company's early shareholders the ability to tap equity holdings well in excess of $1 trillion, could on its own become relevant to the path of the broader economy.

"A $1.5 trillion IPO. The question of what people are going to do with the money now that they have some access to that liquidity is going to become a macro-relevant statistic," Goolsbee said. "We're watching that." DATA-CENTER BACKLASH The US central bank is widely expected to raise interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point at its December 8-9 meeting. Fed policymakers also are wrestling with how the AI boom is influencing the economy. The recent US midterm elections saw AI skepticism emerge at the polls, with municipalities in a number of states approving ballot initiatives that could limit how quickly and where data centers get built, potentially slowing the industry's breakneck evolution. At the same time, the Fed this week held a high-level conference looking at the possible impact on productivity and the labor market should the new technologies diffuse through the economy and reach a potential that Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has characterized as pivotal to US economic leadership. In remarks at an earlier event on Thursday, Goolsbee said it was not yet clear what effect AI will have on productivity or the economy's underlying potential, noting that it took years — even decades — for other general-purpose technologies to change how businesses operated on a broad basis. In the meantime, the Fed will have to cope with short-term effects that so far seem to be inflationary. "The Fed's job is to prevent this thing from overheating the economy," with monetary policy set tight enough to keep demand and supply in balance, Goolsbee said at the event. The Chicago Fed chief did not say if he would support a larger half-percentage-point rate hike at the December meeting, as at least one of his colleagues has advocated, but added that all options were on the table. "The question of how steep the rate path is going to be and if there will be any rate increases should be determined, in my view, by whether you think inflation is going to be heading back to 2 per cent on its own or not," Goolsbee said. "The evidence does not suggest we're on a path back to 2 per cent."

Source: Reuters

Nov 19 : Meta Platforms plans to price its pocket-sized AI device, Muse Charm, at $300 and offer buyers up to 12 months of free 5G data from Verizon, the Information reported on Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter. • Verizon did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment, while a Meta spokesperson said "we're charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we'll have more to share soon" • The device that carries the viral Muse AI agent into the real world was unveiled in September by chief executive Mark Zuckerberg during the company's annual conference • Muse Charm underscores Meta's broader push to reduce its reliance on Apple and Google's operating systems by building its own AI platform

item.title: Diverging Canadian, U.S. interest rate paths weigh on loonie as it trades at 69 cents
item.description: Financial experts say a diverging interest rate path between Canada and the U.S. is weighing on the Canadian dollar, which has dipped below 70 cents US.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: Financial experts say a diverging interest rate path between Canada and the U.S. is weighing on the Canadian dollar, which has dipped below 70 cents US. The Canadian dollar has been falling in recent weeks, now trading at around 69.74 cents US as of Thursday.  “The essential driver of the Canadian dollar exchange rate has been that widening interest rate differential, the spread between short-term U.S. interest rates and short-term Canadian interest rates,” said Shaun Osborne, chief FX strategist at Scotiabank, in an interview. “U.S. interest rates have moved up quite sharply. Canadian interest rates have moved up as well, but not quite as much.”  The Bank of Canada’s benchmark interest rate stands at 2.5 per cent, while in the U.S., the Federal Reserve’s target range is 3.75 per cent to four per cent. Osborne said U.S. interest rates are expected to rise over the next few months.  Minutes released from the Fed’s October meeting suggest it’s likely the central bank will lift its key interest rate by a quarter point next month. Meanwhile, financial market odds of a Bank of Canada rate hike in December stood at roughly 65 per cent as of Thursday, according to LSEG Data & Analytics. Osborne said the decline in the loonie’s relative value is also due to strength in the U.S. dollar, which has been pressuring a number of currencies. “From our perspective, the Canadian dollar looks relatively cheap and we think it offers some value here,” he said.  “But against that you have this very strong underlying trend momentum in the U.S. dollar, with the focus on interest rates. It’s probably going to keep the U.S. dollar trading on the stronger side in the near term at least.”  Looking further ahead, Osborne said U.S. interest rates are likely to fall in late 2027 and into 2028, which should bring “some meaningful compression in that yield differential,” and there is a more positive longer-term outlook for the Canadian dollar.  Sadiq Adatia, chief investment officer of BMO Global Asset Management, said in an interview that trade uncertainty is also a big overhang on Canada’s currency.  “The question mark there still remains that we don’t have a deal yet and people are not likely to be investing significantly in Canada, which means they’re not buying Canadian dollars. That puts a little bit more of a cloud over the Canadian dollar,” he said. Adatia said the U.S. economy is also seeing greater strength with more money flowing into it compared with Canada.  Once Canada and the U.S. hash out a trade agreement, Adatia said the loonie could start to regain ground.      Adatia said currencies often trade above or below their fair value due partly to psychological considerations.  “Now that it’s broken through the 70 cent barrier, there probably is a threshold there that it’s heading lower from that standpoint. Normally, you don’t see it break through a barrier and then just come back again; it goes a little bit further down,” he said. --- Daniel Johnson, The Canadian Press With files from The Associated Press.   This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 19, 2026.

FAST

TOKYO, Nov 20 : Japanese investors sought to buy more than 1.5 trillion yen ($9.40 billion) worth of Anthropic shares at its public listing this week, two people familiar with the offer said. Japanese investors ultimately secured $2.98 billion worth of the shares, a filing showed on Thursday. Anthropic raised $81 billion in total worldwide in what became the world's largest initial public offering on record, eclipsing SpaceX, which raised $75 billion at its listing in June. Market sentiment has turned against AI-related firms in recent months, which sparked speculation that the Claude developer's listing would struggle to win over investors.

Anthropic ultimately priced its offering at $83 per share, above its initial range of $70 to $78. Some Japanese investors saw Anthropic as the frontrunner among AI firms and so justified large orders, said the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the IPO publicly. Other investors sought smaller allocations or sat out the offering altogether, seeing greater prospective returns in semiconductor stocks that have fallen sharply, such as Nvidia and Kioxia, or in waiting for OpenAI’s listing due next year, one of the people said. More than 1,000 individuals sought allotments over 100 million yen, according to a demand survey by Mizuho Securities, part of Mizuho Financial Group, which was among the underwriters of the IPO and arranged the sale of the majority of shares sold in Japan. These applications totalled around 200 billion yen, the survey showed. ($1 = 159.5700 yen)

item.title: China bars Bloomberg reporter from Trump-Xi meet after question on Nvidia
item.description: Annmarie Hordern was denied access to Thursday's trilateral meeting in Shenzhen after asking Trump whether former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had been disloyal to the US ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / China bars Bloomberg reporter from Trump-Xi meet after question on Nvidia

China bars Bloomberg reporter from Trump-Xi meet after question on Nvidia Annmarie Hordern was denied access to Thursday's trilateral meeting in Shenzhen after asking Trump whether former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had been disloyal to the US

Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump arrive for a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on November 19, 2026 in Shenzhen, China | Win McNamee/Pool via REUTERS

AP New York 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 20 2026 | 8:26 AM IST

Listen to This Article

It's a scenario seen every day: A reporter shouts a question out to a leader at an event. The leader either answers or ignores it. In China, though, Bloomberg TV journalist Annmarie Hordern was blocked from a key event by Chinese officials, apparently as retribution for having shouted a question in a way that the government considered rude. Hordern was barred from Thursday's trilateral meeting among President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, after having called out a question during a Trump meeting with Xi. She had asked Trump if former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had been disloyal to the United States.

A White House official said the Chinese insisted the reporter not be allowed in despite the White House having pushed for admission. The official insisted on speaking on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity around the issue. The White House did not immediately respond to a query about what steps it took to advocate for the reporter. Jacqui Heinrich, president of the White House Correspondents' Association, said on X that it was "commendable that the WH is advocating for press access". A pool report from the incident said the Chinese "have passed along a message that yelling questions is considered extremely rude and we will be pulled from the room if we do so".

Also Read

India must turn China trade dependence into domestic value addition premium

China's Foreign Ministry did not respond to a request for comment from The Associated Press, and an email to Bloomberg seeking comment was not immediately returned. The incident, which reflected the way China typically seeks to tightly control news events, recalled a previous one in 2022, in which a White House pool reporter said she was knocked off balance after being yanked by her backpack when she tried to shout a question to President Joe Biden. The question was about human rights ahead of a meeting between Biden and Xi in Bali, Indonesia. The reporter lost balance without falling and was pushed towards the door, a pool report said at the time. Two White House staff members intervened and said the producer should be left alone.

China's approach to journalists, particularly foreign media, has long been chilly and uneven. In recent decades, international reporters have been expelled both for their coverage and for perceived misbehavior during news events. Resident correspondents are occasionally detained and questioned -- and in some cases in past years, compelled to sign "self-criticism" reports -- for showing up where the government doesn't want them to be. Chinese journalists who stray from the party line can face even more stringent measures, including censorship, dismissal and at times even imprisonment.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: TD report examines financial health of Canadian households
item.description: As Canadians grapple with elevated rates of unemployment and inflation, as well as the fallout from an ongoing trade war with the U.S., a new report suggests most households are still finding ways to ...
item.dc:creator: Jordan Fleguel
item.content:encoded: As Canadians grapple with elevated rates of unemployment and inflation, as well as the fallout from an ongoing trade war with the U.S., a new report suggests most households are still finding ways to make ends meet, despite a number of troubling economic data points. “Canadian consumers are holding up reasonably well,” wrote Maria Solovieva, CFA and economist, in a report released Thursday by TD Economics. The report noted that real consumer spending grew at a nearly three per cent pace through the first half of 2026, suggesting Canadians have remained resilient in the face of numerous economic challenges. “But solid spending growth masks pockets of financial strain, particularly in Ontario,” Solovieva wrote. “A closer look at several indicators – insolvencies, delinquencies, and mortgage arrears – reveals a mixed picture, with some measures showing signs of stabilizing while others continue to deteriorate.” Weakness in Ontario In Canada’s largest province, the current financial strain on Canadians is “most visible,” according to the report. “Ontario stands out with mortgage arrears nearly tripling from pre-pandemic norms and approaching their Global Financial Crisis (GFC) peak. This reflects elevated mortgage balances and greater sensitivity to borrowing costs,” it said. Mortgage arrears have also risen, to a lesser extent, in British Columbia, as both provinces experienced significant home price gains during the pandemic period, the report noted, leaving many homeowners with larger mortgage balances relative to income. While the pace of growth in B.C. mortgage arears has slowed more recently, the rate has continued to climb in Ontario, hitting 0.34 per cent in August. That’s nearly triple its pre-pandemic level of around 0.12 per cent and approaching the 0.43 per cent peak during the GFC, according to the report. “Still, perspective matters. Even at today’s elevated rate, roughly one in 300 Ontario mortgages is in arrears,” said Solovieva. “These missed payments do not necessarily translate into more severe financial distress or credit losses. Many borrowers retain substantial home equity, giving both households and lenders some flexibility to manage financial difficulties.” Those who are most vulnerable now are homeowners who purchased property during the 2021 and 2022 housing peak, when prices were highest and “equity cushions may be thinnest,” the report noted. Eyes on the labour market Across Canada, but particularly in Ontario, Canadians are faced with the combination of high living costs and a weakening labour market, which has hit some of the province’s traditional manufacturing centres hardest. “Notably, more than 35 per cent of people living in households in Oshawa, Windsor and Hamilton report difficulties meeting their financial needs – the highest among Canada’s largest cities,” wrote Solovieva. “Unemployment rates in all three cities are also above the national average, underscoring how labour market weakness is compounding existing affordability pressures in some regions.” At a national level, the labour market will continue to be a key indicator of the financial health of Canadians going forward, the report said. Earlier this month, Statistics Canada reported that the country’s unemployment rate rose to 6.7 per cent in October. It marked the third consecutive month of net job losses for the Canadian economy. ‘Little reason to sound the alarm’ TD says it expects stronger economic and labour market growth next year. However, forecasting accurately is difficult given the uncertainty surrounding Canada’s trading relationship with the U.S. as well as ongoing global conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East. “Despite these vulnerabilities, we see little reason to sound the alarm bell over a broader deterioration in household credit performance. Ontario’s mortgage arrears are rising but are forecast to decline next year as the economy improves,” Solovieva argued. “If weak hiring gives way to widespread job losses… mortgage arrears could rise further and remain elevated for longer, but with stronger economic growth and a recovering labour market in our forecast, households in Ontario and across Canada are expected to bend but not break.”

US was warned of telecom security risks years before Salt Typhoon

FAST

Nov 19 : The US government was warned in a report it commissioned about major national security risks from weaknesses in the country's telecom networks in 2022, two years before sweeping Chinese-linked cyberespionage known as Salt Typhoon. The report commissioned by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency said US telecommunications networks contained "major structural vulnerabilities" and could be compromised from anywhere in the world. US officials have previously alleged that hackers targeted nine telecom companies, including Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile and Lumen, during the 2024 Salt Typhoon campaign and stole telephone audio intercepts and a large tranche of call-record data. The report, disclosed as part of a lawsuit, has been reviewed by Reuters.

Details of the report were first reported by Bloomberg News on Thursday. The June 2022 report described US telecom infrastructure as one in a "perilous and untenable situation," and added that international interconnects could provide attackers with "trusted" access. "The fact that US national networks can be readily compromised from anywhere in the world is not yet widely understood." CISA withheld the report from public release for four years and resisted congressional pressure to publish it, according to Bloomberg News. The agency did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Ron Wyden, a Democratic senator from Oregon, pushed for the release of the report last year. He had said in a statement, "Congress would have had ample time to require mandatory cybersecurity standards for phone companies, in time to prevent the Salt Typhoon hacks" had the report been made public when it was first written.

Source: Reuters

FAST

Nov 19 : Amazon said on Thursday that a New York City Council bill under consideration, requiring last-mile delivery operators to be licensed by the city and directly employ workers rather than contract the work, "could add up to $5" to each order. The ecommerce major added that it might be forced to consider moving operations outside the city if the bill passes. • Amazon told New York City customers that the council was weighing Intro 518, a bill sponsored by member Tiffany Caban, which could affect how it delivers packages and groceries and push prices up • The company said it works with a network of small delivery businesses that it would no longer be able to work with if the legislation passes • It also said moving operations outside the city would likely mean slower and more expensive deliveries for millions of customers • "We are crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs," Council Speaker Julie Menin told Reuters in a emailed statement, calling Amazon's campaign "deceptive"

Source: Reuters

item.description: Formula One's push to turn its rapid global growth into a broader lifestyle business took another step on Thursday with the announcement of a long-term partnership that will make Nike the sport's ...
item.content:encoded:
Motor racing-Nike to become Formula One's official apparel and uniform partner Formula One's push to turn its rapid global growth into a broader lifestyle business took another step on Thursday with the announcement of a long-term partnership that will make Nike the sport's official apparel and uniform supplier from 2027. Reuters | Updated: 20-11-2026 06:39 IST | Created: 20-11-2026 06:39 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Formula One's push to turn its rapid global growth into a broader lifestyle business took another step on Thursday with the announcement of a long-term partnership that will make Nike the sport's official apparel and uniform supplier from 2027. Nike will create co-branded uniforms for staff at Formula One events worldwide, as well as footwear, apparel and accessories for fans. Financial terms were not disclosed. The partnership will also cover F1 Academy, Formula One's all-female development series, where Nike will provide performance-focused apparel and support athlete innovation initiatives. The collaboration will make its first public appearance with a limited Las Vegas Grand Prix x Nike capsule collection, available on Friday at the F1 Hub and Nike stores in Las Vegas ahead of the Saturday night race. Formula One has increasingly pursued partnerships beyond traditional motorsport categories as it seeks to engage younger audiences and extend its appeal across fashion, entertainment and culture. "Formula 1 is experiencing unprecedented global growth," Formula One President and Chief Executive Stefano Domenicali said in a statement, describing Nike as an ideal partner for the championship's next phase. Nike President and Chief Executive Elliott Hill said Formula One's emphasis on competition, speed and innovation matched the sportswear company's athlete-focused approach. "Together, we have an incredible opportunity to bring new energy to the sport, serve its athletes and inspire fans around the world," Hill said.

item.title: How India taxes foreign investors' share gains and how peers compare
item.description: India charges foreign portfolio investors the same capital gains tax as residents, while several large markets exempt them; the government is now examining the issue ...
item.dc:creator: Vedant Vichare
item.content:encoded: The finance ministry is examining calls to scrap the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax on foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), but any decision will come only in the Budget, Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) chairman Ravi Agrawal said on November 16. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has reportedly recommended the move, Reuters reported on November 2. The recommendation is not binding, and the Union Budget is due in February 2027. What India charges foreign investors India taxes FPIs on listed equities at the same rates as residents. Gains on shares held for more than 12 months are taxed at 12.5 per cent above Rs 1.25 lakh a year, and gains on shares held for up to 12 months at 20 per cent. Foreign investors also pay securities transaction tax (STT) of 0.1 per cent on both the purchase and the sale of shares taken for delivery, whether or not they make a profit.  China exempts foreign investors from corporate income tax on gains from shares of mainland Chinese companies, known as A-shares, according to PwC’s analysis of two notices issued jointly by its finance ministry, tax administration and securities regulator in November 2014. Foreigners mainly reach these shares through Stock Connect, a trading link with Hong Kong, or as licensed institutional investors (QFII or RQFII) with no business presence in China. The exemption applies to gains from November 17, 2014, and earlier gains remain taxable. Such gains are otherwise taxed at 10 per cent, and the exemption is temporary in name: it rests on an administrative circular, not a law, and has been in place for more than 10 years, KPMG Luxembourg noted in March 2026.What the government has said Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on November 2 that the government would consider the representations it has received on the capital gains tax structure, and that India needs capital to sustain growth. Agrawal said on November 16 that points raised by stakeholders were being examined and that “Any decision would be taken only in the Budget”. The case for relief Saurabh Mukherjea, founder and chief investment officer of Marcellus Investment Managers, says India is an outlier. “No other large market charges capital gain tax to foreigners,” he told Business Standard. He says India does not follow the usual practice of leaving foreign investors to be taxed in their home country. Mukherjea says the 12.5 per cent headline rate understates the burden. By his account, adding STT, surcharge and GST brings the effective rate to about 15 per cent, and the cash that foreign funds set aside for future tax takes the overall tax cost to 16-16.5 per cent. He says the MSCI India index, which foreign funds use as a benchmark for Indian equities, has returned as little as 7 per cent over 10 years in dollar terms after netting off taxes. He says the issue did not matter before 2018, when long-term gains were not taxed, and that foreign selling picked up after the 2024 increase. He puts the outflow at about $70 billion over two years and describes artificial intelligence (AI)-related swings as transient, with tax as a structural factor. The case for a targeted approach Akhil Chandna, partner and global people solutions leader at Grant Thornton Bharat, does not back a blanket exemption, meaning no capital gains tax at all for foreign investors. “I am not saying abolishing capital gains tax across the board,” he says in his written note. He suggests India could examine whether genuine long-term institutional FPIs should get an exemption or a concessional rate, while short-term speculative gains stay taxed, subject to holding-period and anti-abuse conditions. He also recommends, as a pre-Budget suggestion, that the government review and rationalise the framework so that it is more competitive for foreign investors. A full exemption for foreign investors, he adds, raises questions of tax neutrality when domestic investors continue to pay. Chandna also says India’s rates on its own residents are lower than those in several developed economies, though higher than in Singapore, Hong Kong and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Pre-Budget consultations are on, and Agrawal said the outcome would be known on February 1. Whether any relief is limited to foreign investors or also covers Indian investors will be visible then.

item.title: Somalia orders UAE ambassador to leave, citing 'invasion'
item.description: "Measures will be taken against anyone who cooperates with UAE in the invasion against Somalia," Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud said in a broadcast on the state-run news agency on Thursday (Nov 19).
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Somalia orders UAE ambassador to leave, citing 'invasion'

"Measures will be taken against anyone who cooperates with UAE in the invasion against Somalia," Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud said in a broadcast on the state-run news agency on Thursday (Nov 19).

Soldiers with their armored vehicles near a checkpoint in Mogadishu. The UAE has helped fund and train Somalia's military and backed ports and other commercial ventures. (AP Photo/Farah Abdi Warsameh, File)

FAST

MOGADISHU: Somalia ordered the United Arab Emirates ambassador on Thursday (Nov 19) to leave the country within 72 hours and withdrew its own envoy from Abu Dhabi, accusing the Emirates of unspecified violations of Somalia's sovereignty that amounted to an "open invasion". "Measures will be taken against anyone who cooperates with UAE in the invasion against Somalia," Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud said in a broadcast on the state-run news agency. "All Somalis are urged to defend their country and unite against the open invasion of the UAE against the sovereignty, security, land and unity of Somalis." The minister did not elaborate on the actions the UAE had taken that had provoked Somalia's response.

In a speech on Tuesday, Somalia's President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud had accused the UAE of giving economic and political support to some regional Somali governments to oppose the federal government. There was no immediate response from the UAE foreign ministry. The UAE, which has helped fund and train Somalia's military in the past and has backed ports and other commercial ventures there, has long denied meddling in the country's affairs.

Related:

UAE investigators say flydubai co-pilot was planning 'terrorist act'

In January, Somalia said it had ended all agreements with the UAE, including port deals and defence and security cooperation, accusing the UAE of undermining its national sovereignty. Three self-governing Somali regions that have close relations with the United Arab Emirates dismissed that move at the time. The UAE has long leveraged its wealth to expand its influence across the Horn of Africa, using a mix of economic, military and diplomatic clout to assert regional power. For decades Somalia's federal government has had only limited authority across the country, and has failed to defeat Islamist militants, despite years of international support, including African peacekeepers and US air strikes. The UAE trained hundreds of Somali troops from 2014 to 2018, and still covers salaries and provides logistics for around 3,400 Somali military police and special forces troops in and around the capital, according to senior Somali sources. It has also forged bonds directly with regional governments, committing hundreds of millions of dollars to ports and military infrastructure on the coast along global shipping routes.

Source: Reuters/ht

Cartesi to Close Vote on CTSI MinterRole Renunciation on November 25th Less than 1 min read

CTSIUSD

Cartesi will close voting on November 25th on a proposal to renounce the remaining MinterRole permissions in the CTSI token contract. The voting period runs from November 18th–25th following a 21-day consultation. Refer to the official tweet by CTSI:

Cartesi @cartesiproject

Itâ€™s time to vote! The proposal to renounce the remaining MinterRole permissions on the $CTSI token contract is now open for voting, following a 21-day consultation period. Review the details and cast your vote here: https://t.co/qfaEWpIK5k Voting period 🗓ï¸ Nov 18 - Nov 25 pic.twitter.com/EywpwXewyy

Nov 18, 2026

CTSI Info Cartesi (CTSI) is a blockchain project aiming to make the development and deployment of decentralized applications (DApps) more practical and scalable. It does this by enabling smart contracts to run off-chain computations in a Linux environment, which opens up the possibility to use mainstream programming languages and software, as well as access larger amounts of data more efficiently. The fundamental piece of technology behind Cartesi is the Descartes SDK, a software development kit that provides a set of tools and services to help developers build scalable and secure DApps. With Descartes, computations can be intensive and incorporate complex business logic as they are executed off-chain in a Linux environment. The Cartesi token (CTSI) serves multiple utility purposes within the Cartesi ecosystem. It is used as a staking mechanism in the network's Proof-of-Stake (PoS) consensus algorithm, and also as a means to pay for computational resources within the network. In addition, it's used in the network's incentive system for data availability and computation verification.

Nym to Host Community Call on November 19th Less than 1 min read

Nym will hold a community call with David Schwartz of the Litecoin Foundation on November 19th at 14:00 UTC, streamed on YouTube and Twitch. The discussion will cover MWEB confidential transactions, optional versus default privacy, and Litecoin’s approach to financial privacy. Refer to the official tweet by NYM:

Nym @nym

NYM Community Call with David Schwartz from @litecoin November 19 | 14:00 UTC Set Reminderâ¤µï¸ YT: https://t.co/ygjVmbgYDX Twitch: https://t.co/B6tdAZlRjp 🪙 How MWEB brought privacy to Litecoin 🔐 Optional vs default: the design choice 👩â€💻 Litecoin's take on financial privacyâ€¦ pic.twitter.com/XHZQwuZ4QY

Nov 19, 2026

NYM Info Users employ NYM tokens to gain access to the mixnet, consequently improving the privacy of their data. NYM is also used as a reward for mix nodes in exchange for their services in traffic mixing and privacy assurance for Nym network users. Fees accumulated in NYM are directed to a reward pool and later distributed amongst mix nodes, based on their performance and reputation. Each mix node's reputation is quantified in NYM tokens. Moreover, users have the option to delegate their NYM tokens to mix nodes. This action serves as a validation of a mix node's reputation and grants the user a portion of the mix node's rewards. Users are encouraged to delegate their NYM to nodes that consistently deliver quality services as it increases their likelihood of earning rewards. However, it should be noted that NYM is not a general-purpose payment mechanism or a typical cryptocurrency, such as Bitcoin. Its utilization is exclusively intended for activities within the Nym network.

item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot, made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday following a record USD 81.34 billion initial public offering (IPO), securing a ...
item.content:encoded:
Anthropic makes Nasdaq debut after record USD 81 billion IPO, secures USD 1.5 trillion valuation Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot, made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday following a record USD 81.34 billion initial public offering (IPO), securing a valuation of approximately USD 1.5 trillion, according to Reuters. ANI | Updated: 19-11-2026 20:47 IST | Created: 19-11-2026 20:47 IST

Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday. (Photo:Nasdaq). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot, made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday following a record USD 81.34 billion initial public offering (IPO), securing a valuation of approximately USD 1.5 trillion, according to Reuters. The landmark public offering comes amid growing investor interest in artificial intelligence companies, even as concerns persist over elevated valuations, the sustainability of AI-related investments and the potential emergence of a market bubble. According to the company's IPO details, Anthropic offered 980 million shares at USD 83 apiece, raising approximately USD 81.34 billion through the public offering. The company is listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the proposed ticker symbol 'ANT'. Reuters reported that the record IPO represents a major test of Wall Street's confidence in the AI boom, as investors weigh the technology's potential to transform the global economy against concerns over financial risks and its broader implications for humanity. The offering also comes alongside the latest earnings announcement from AI chipmaker Nvidia, with both developments serving as significant indicators of investor confidence in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence industry. According to the financial details provided in the IPO filing, Anthropic reported revenue of USD 33.24 billion, while its net loss stood at approximately USD 104.04 billion. The company reported total assets of USD 154.32 billion and total liabilities of USD 146.68 billion, highlighting the scale of its financial operations. Anthropic, led by Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei, had approximately 5,300 employees as of September 30, 2026. The IPO details also showed that the company had approximately 7.43 billion shares outstanding, while the offering included around 23.65 million shareholder shares. The record listing marks a significant milestone for the artificial intelligence industry, with Anthropic's market valuation placing it among the world's most highly valued technology companies. (ANI)

item.title: US jobless claims rise by 1,000 to 203,000, continuing claims climb by 70,000
item.description: The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits rose by 1,000 to a seasonally adjusted 203,000 in the week ended November 14, while the number continuing to receive benefits ...
item.content:encoded:
US jobless claims rise by 1,000 to 203,000, continuing claims climb by 70,000 The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits rose by 1,000 to a seasonally adjusted 203,000 in the week ended November 14, while the number continuing to receive benefits climbed by 70,000 to 1.763 million in the preceding week, the US Department of Labor said on Thursday. ANI | Updated: 19-11-2026 19:41 IST | Created: 19-11-2026 19:41 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits rose by 1,000 to a seasonally adjusted 203,000 in the week ended November 14, while the number continuing to receive benefits climbed by 70,000 to 1.763 million in the preceding week, the US Department of Labor said on Thursday. “In the week ending November 14, the advance figure for seasonally adjusted initial claims was 203,000, an increase of 1,000 from the previous week's revised level,” the department said in its weekly unemployment insurance claims report. It revised the previous week’s figure up to 202,000 from 200,000. The four-week moving average of initial claims, which smooths out weekly fluctuations, rose by 2,000 to 197,750 from a revised 195,750. Initial claims, which track new applications for unemployment benefits, were below the 222,000 recorded in the comparable week a year earlier. “The advance number for seasonally adjusted insured unemployment during the week ending November 7 was 1,763,000, an increase of 70,000 from the previous week's revised level,” the department said. It revised the prior week’s figure down to 1.693 million from 1.697 million. Continuing claims count people who remain on unemployment benefits after an initial week of aid. The figures are reported with a one-week lag relative to initial claims. Their four-week average rose by 10,250 to 1.717 million, while the weekly figure remained below the 1.949 million recorded a year earlier. Before seasonal adjustment, new claims under state programmes fell by 11,941, or 5.7 per cent, to 197,492 in the week ended November 14. The department said seasonal patterns had pointed to a decline of 12,534, or 6 per cent. The seasonally adjusted insured unemployment rate, which measures the share of workers covered by unemployment insurance who are receiving benefits, held at 1.1 per cent in the week ended November 7, compared with 1.3 per cent a year earlier. (ANI)

item.title: Indonesian miners scramble for clarity as Prabowo seeks greater state share
item.description: Miners in Indonesia, the world’s biggest exporter of thermal coal, nickel and tin, are scrambling to decipher President Prabowo Subianto’s call for the st
item.dc:creator: Mining.com
item.content:encoded: Miners in Indonesia, the world’s biggest exporter of thermal coal, nickel and tin, are scrambling to decipher President Prabowo Subianto’s call for the state to secure greater benefits from mining operations, warning that the uncertainty could deter investment in the resource-rich nation. The comments add to concerns among investors over policy uncertainty in Southeast Asia’s largest economy – home to the world’s largest gold mine and the biggest known nickel reserves – which has already been rattled by warnings from international credit ratings agencies and the prospect of MSCI excluding the country from its stock market indexes. Indonesia’s energy stock index .JKENERGY, which includes shares of coal miners, has dropped 4.1% since Prabowo’s weekend comments – while the basic materials stock index .JKBASIC, which covers miners of other minerals, has lost 6.2%. Prabowo, speaking on Saturday, said he had instructed ministers to ensure the state receives at least “70% of the benefits from all mining permits” and added that, if necessary, the state should “take over stakes” in companies in Indonesia. The president did not spell out what constituted “benefits” or how the 70% would be calculated, leaving miners and analysts trying to assess whether he was referring to profits, revenue, taxes and royalties, or a broader measure of the state’s economic benefit. “We are still examining what President Prabowo meant by his intention for 70% of mining sector proceeds to go into state coffers,” Sudirman Widhy Hartono, chairman of the Association of Mining Professionals, told Reuters. He said the industry was awaiting a more detailed explanation from the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources. The ministry did not respond to a request from Reuters for comment. A spokesperson for the president did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The mining sector, especially in nickel and coal, is already struggling with tighter production quotas and rising costs. French miner Eramet, which was forced to halt operations for several months due to a lower mining quota, is planning to sell some stake in its Indonesian nickel mine. “The mere uncertainty surrounding definitions is enough to delay new investment decisions,” said Fauzan Luthfi Djamal, mining analyst with brokerage Mirae Asset Sekuritas Indonesia. “Foreign partners involved in nickel downstreaming are likely re-evaluating project returns, while financing costs could potentially rise.” Mineral-rich Indonesia had seen massive investment in its nickel processing sector following a raw nickel export ban in 2020, and a similar ban on other minerals in 2023. Impact on companies Fauzan said the state’s objective of increasing revenue from natural resources is “understandable” but the challenge is designing a scheme that captures windfall gains without stifling business or deterring new investment. Sudirman said data from coal mining companies showed total state revenue can reach around 32% of total sales, while companies earn profits of less than 10% – which means government revenue is more than three times company profit. Depending on how the 70% “benefit” is calculated, Fauzan estimated net profits for privately owned miners could be cut by as much as half, while mines operating under special mining licences could see profits fall by up to a third. Fauzan said the quickest route would probably be through higher royalties, with the government having previously considered increases for gold, copper, silver, nickel and tin. Other possibilities include additional levies or requiring state equity participation when mining licences are extended or converted. Indonesia had earlier this year shelved plans to impose windfall taxes on coal and nickel exports and increase royalties on some mining companies. In May, Prabowo said exports of coal, palm oil and ferroalloys would be controlled by state-run Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia to combat exports being under-invoiced. The proposal was subsequently scaled back, with the agency saying its initial role would be as a centralised data collector. In August, Prabowo also announced a commodities exchange and said Indonesia should set its own prices rather than follow global benchmarks. “Prabowo often issues directives,” said Bhima Yudhistira Adhinegara, an economist at the Center of Economics and Law Studies think tank. “Yet the technical regulations are never prepared beforehand … we’re seeing this happen again.” (Reporting by Fransiska Nangoy and Bernadette Christina; Writing by Gibran Peshimam; Editing by Raju Gopalakrishnan)
